title: Partition Suit (Batwara Mamla) in Bangladesh for NRBs: How to Claim Your Inherited Land from USA, UK & Canada (2026)
metaTitle: Partition Suit Bangladesh: Batwara Mamla Guide for NRBs 2026
metaDescription: How Non-Resident Bangladeshis in USA, UK & Canada can file a Partition Suit (বাটোয়ারা মামলা) in Bangladesh without travelling. Court fees, Saham shares & injunctions.
keywords: how to file partition suit from abroad bangladesh
heroIntro: One of the most frequent legal heartbreaks for Non-Resident Bangladeshis (NRBs) in the United States, United Kingdom, and Canada is being denied their legitimate inheritance shares in ancestral family property by relatives back home. When co-sharers refuse mutual amicable settlement, conceal land income, or attempt unauthorized construction and third-party sales, the definitive legal remedy is filing a formal **Partition Suit (বাটোয়ারা মামলা)** under the Partition Act 1893 and the Code of Civil Procedure 1908. Crucially, an overseas heir does NOT need to reside in Bangladesh to litigate and secure their court decree.

quickAnswer.heading: Partition Suit for Expats: Core Legal Steps
points: Execute a Special Power of Attorney abroad appointing a trusted representative or lawyer in Bangladesh.
Collect all ancestral land records: CS, SA, RS, BS Khatians, Warishan Certificate, and Mutation Porchas.
Send a formal Legal Notice demanding partition by mutual metes and bounds.
File the Partition Suit in the Senior Assistant Judge or Sub-Judge Court having local territorial jurisdiction.
Obtain an ad-interim Injunction under Order 39 Rules 1 & 2 of the CPC to freeze land transfers and construction.
Obtain a Preliminary Decree declaring your specific fractional share (Saham / সাহাম).
Execute the Final Decree through a Court Advocate Commissioner who demarcates physical boundaries on the ground.

sections.h2: What is a Partition Suit (বাটোয়ারা মামলা)?
sections.content:
A Partition Suit is a civil action filed under the Partition Act, 1893 and the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC) by a co-owner or co-sharer seeking judicial division of undivided joint family property (সহ-অংশীদারী সম্পত্তি বন্টন) according to their lawful statutory share.

Under both Islamic law (Farayez) and Hindu law (Dayabhaga), heirs become joint tenants upon the death of the predecessor. Until a registered partition deed (রেজিস্ট্রিকৃত আপস বন্টননামা) is executed or a civil court passes a partition decree, every co-sharer holds an undivided interest across every square inch of the property.

sections.h2: Grounds for Filing: When Mutual Settlement Fails
sections.content:
Expats should institute a partition suit immediately when faced with:

  • Co-sharer brothers or uncles occupying prime road-front land while relegating overseas siblings to inaccessible back-plots.
  • Attempts by local relatives to sell specific demarcated portions of undivided property to third-party developers without your consent.
  • Refusal to share rental income from commercial buildings, markets, or agricultural leaseholds in Bangladesh.
  • Denial of female heirs' (sisters/daughters) shares in violation of statutory inheritance law.

sections.h2: Can an NRB File from Abroad Without Visiting Bangladesh?
sections.content: Yes. Under Order III Rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, any appearance, application, or act in court may be made by the party in person or by his recognized agent. An expatriate living in New York, London, or Toronto can execute a Special Power of Attorney before the local Bangladesh Embassy, have it verified by MOFA and stamped at the DC office in Dhaka, authorizing their attorney or engaged Supreme Court advocate to file the plaint, sign affidavits, and attend all hearing dates.

sections.h2: Determining Court Fees: Fixed vs Ad-Valorem Fees
sections.content:
Under the Court-fees Act, 1870, the fee structure depends on whether the plaintiff is in joint physical/constructive possession:

  • Constructive Possession (সহ-দখল বিদ্যমান থাকলে): If your title is undisputed and you are treated as a co-sharer in constructive joint possession, a nominal fixed court fee (currently BDT 300 to BDT 1,000 under Schedule II Article 17) is payable.
  • Complete Ouster or Denied Title (দখলচ্যুতি বা স্বত্ব অস্বীকার): If the defendants dispute your title or have completely ousted you from possession, the suit transforms into a suit for declaration of title and recovery of possession, attracting ad-valorem court fees calculated on the market valuation of your share (up to statutory ceiling limits).

sections.h2: Two Critical Stages: Preliminary Decree vs Final Decree
sections.content:
Unlike ordinary civil suits, a Partition Suit proceeds through two distinct judicial phases:

  1. Preliminary Decree (প্রাথমিক ডিক্রি): The Civil Court examines the chain of title, hears evidence, determines the genealogical tree (Waris), and adjudicates the exact mathematical fraction (Saham / সাহাম) belonging to each party. No physical demarcation occurs at this stage.
  2. Final Decree (চূড়ান্ত ডিক্রি): After the preliminary decree is passed, the court allows the parties a window to partition mutually. If they fail, any party can apply for the appointment of an Advocate Commissioner (তদন্ত কমিশনার) to visit the land, survey boundaries with government Amin, draw partition maps (চিঠাকাটা), and submit a final allotment report for court confirmation.

sections.h2: Securing an Injunction (Order 39 CPC) to Halt Land Sales
sections.content:
The biggest threat to overseas heirs during litigation is defendants hurriedly selling plots to third parties or erecting permanent multi-story structures. To neutralize this threat:

Simultaneously with filing the plaint, file an application for temporary injunction under Order XXXIX Rules 1 & 2 read with Section 151 of the CPC. The court can issue an ad-interim injunction restraining the defendants from altering the nature or character of the suit land, transferring shares, or creating third-party encumbrances pending final disposal.

sections.h2: Court Commissioner Survey & Physical Boundary Demarcation
sections.content:
The Advocate Commissioner plays the pivotal role in the final decree stage:

  • Inspects the physical terrain in the presence of all parties and local village elders.
  • Ensures that road access, drainage, and property valuation equity are maintained across all allocated Sahams.
  • If the property is indivisible without destroying its utility (e.g., a single small shop or narrow house), the court may invoke Section 2 of the Partition Act 1893 to order a public auction among co-sharers or third parties, distributing the cash proceeds.

sections.h2: Execution Suit (জারী মামলা) & Police Assistance for Possession
sections.content:
Once the Final Decree is sealed, if aggressive relatives refuse to surrender physical possession of your demarcated plot:

  1. File an Execution Case (বন্টন ডিক্রি জারী মামলা) under Order XXI of the CPC.
  2. The court issues a writ of possession and directs the Court Nazir, accompanied by police personnel, to enter the land, erect boundary pillars, and deliver vacant physical possession to your attorney.
  3. Any resistance constitutes contempt of court and criminal obstruction under the Penal Code 1860.

faqs.question: How long does a Partition Suit take in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: A contested partition suit typically takes between 2 to 4 years to complete both the preliminary and final decree stages in the trial court. However, obtaining a temporary injunction happens in the earliest weeks of litigation.

faqs.question: Can my brothers sell my deceased father's land while I live in the USA without my signature?
faqs.answer: No. Under Bangladeshi law, any sale deed executed by one co-sharer without the consent of other legal heirs only conveys their own fractional share; it cannot legally transfer your undivided share.

faqs.question: Do sisters have equal rights to file a partition suit in Bangladesh?
faqs.answer: Absolutely. Under Muslim succession law, daughters inherit specific fixed shares (Farayez), and under the Partition Act, any female heir has full legal standing to file a partition suit independently.

faqs.question: What happens if a co-sharer builds a house on joint land before partition?
faqs.answer: Construction on undivided joint land does not confer title to that specific spot. In the final decree, the court commissioner can allot the structure with adjustment of land value or order demolition if built fraudulently in bad faith.

faqs.question: Can I settle out of court after filing a partition suit?
faqs.answer: Yes. At any stage before the final decree, parties can enter into a Solenama (আপসনামা / compromise petition) under Order XXIII Rule 3 CPC, and the court will dispose of the suit based on the agreed terms.
